newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU executive defends move on British pubs.
newsitem.headline: EU executive defends move on British pubs.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday defended its legal action against British rules it says effectively keep foreign beers out of public houses.

The Commission met with officials from Britain's Department of Trade and Industry, who were in Brussels to argue that the EU executive's action threatened rules on so-called "guest beers" aimed to improve access for smaller breweries to the pubs and break the monopoly of bigger breweries.
"Most of the opposition to this action from the UK is based on fundamental misunderstandings," a Commission spokeswoman said.
"The Commission does not want at all to see the British guest beers rules to be scrapped...We share the objective of promoting access for smaller breweries to tied pubs."
The Commission in July opened the second of three stages of infringement proceedings against London. If it does not gain satisfaction the Commission can haul it before the European Court of Justice.
Under Britain's system of tied houses public houses are tied to a particular brewer, but are obliged to sell one "guest beer" from an outside brewery.
The Commission says that the fact that these guest beers have to be cask conditionned effectively rules out most foreign beers, notably artisanal beers made by small breweries.
